title: Find K Closest Elements
statement:
You are given an array `arr` of `n` integers sorted in non-decreasing order, an integer `k` and a target value `x`. The target does not have to be present in the array.

Pick the `k` elements of `arr` that are closest to `x`, where the distance of a value `v` is `|v - x|`. If two elements are equally close, the **smaller value** is considered closer. Print the chosen elements in ascending order.
inputFormat:
The first line contains three integers `n`, `k` and `x`.
The second line contains `n` integers: the sorted array `arr`.
outputFormat: Print `k` space-separated integers in ascending order.
constraints: arr is sorted in non-decreasing order (duplicates are allowed)

examples.explanation: The distances to 10 are 9, 6, 2, 1, 2, 5, 10. The three smallest are 1 (value 9) and the tie of 2 (values 8 and 12), so the answer is 8 9 12.
Both 5 and 7 are at distance 1 from 6. The tie goes to the smaller value, 5.
The target is beyond the end of the array, so the closest elements are the last two.

hints: Because the array is sorted, the k closest elements always form one contiguous window. You only need to find where it starts.
The window start can be any index from 0 to n - k. Compare the two ends of a candidate window starting at mid: arr[mid] and arr[mid + k].
If x - arr[mid] > arr[mid + k] - x, then arr[mid] is farther than arr[mid + k] and the window must move right. Otherwise it stays or moves left, so binary search on the start.
